messages:
sam-support: FYI MaplePay hit a bunch of customer 5xx and long tail timeouts this morning.
sam-support: Customers reporting p95+ requests timing out at our gateway, ~10-30s, then 502/504. Escalated from CSE. :grimacing:
alex-oncall: I see an alert: continuous-batcher queue depth > 95% for 4 workers in prod-west. s0->s2. What was the recent deploy window? any config changes? 
ben-runtime: No deploys to batcher in the last 6 hours. We did change default batching window from 20ms -> 40ms for throughput testing earlier today (AB test). Could explain bigger batches and backlog.
maria-sre: That matches. Increased batching window + steady ingress -> backlog. Also seeing many requests with longer input lengths from MaplePay (document summarization). KV cache warm-ups increased per-request service time.
alex-oncall: Got logs. snippet:
```
2026-03-17T08:12:03Z gateway: request_enqueue depth=798 max_depth=800 tenant=maplepay latency_wait=210ms
2026-03-17T08:12:34Z batcher: dequeue_wait=1200ms shard=3 batch_size=64 total_kv_miss=58
2026-03-17T08:12:38Z gateway: request_timeout -> 504 route=/v1/generate tenant=maplepay
```
ben-runtime: That batch_size=64 is suspicious given model kv cache pressure. With 40ms window we might be accumulating many small but slow requests into big batches; then one slow request blocks the GPU and pushes queue depth to limit.
kevin-eng: Short-term mitigation ideas:
- revert batching window to 20ms for maplpay tenant (or global) via feature flag
- bump requestQueue.maxDepth for MaplePay to 1200
- enable immediate-dequeue policy for their route (break big batches into smaller ones)
Anyone object to doing all three in parallel for 30m? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria-sre: Do the queue bump + immediate-dequeue first (least disruptive). Reverting window requires runtime rollback and more QA. I'll apply queue bump and policy change via control plane.
alex-oncall: I'll open a support note to MaplePay telling them we're investigating and to expect transient retries; give ETA 30m. Sam, can you gather repro steps and a small load test for eng-runtime? Include content sizes.
sam-support: On it. Repro steps:
1) send 300 concurrent requests spread across 10 clients mimicking MaplePay: prompt sizes 1k-2.5k tokens (docs).
2) set rate to 250 rps ramp -> steady for 60s.
3) header X-tenant: maplepay and route /v1/generate with model=redwood-3b.
Expected: queue depth climbs, p95 latency increases, some 504s within 60-90s.
ben-runtime: Running a quick repro in staging now. Also checking guardian logs for eviction behavior. If deferred-evictions kick in we saw tail timeouts before.
sre-bot: alert: continuous-batcher.prod-west.queue_depth >= 0.95 (fired)
kevin-eng: Commands I'm about to run (control-plane):
```
# bump queue depth for MaplePay
curl -XPOST https://control-plane.internal/api/tenants/maplepay/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"requestQueue": {"maxDepth": 1200, "deferredEvictions": false}}'

# enable immediate dequeue small-batches
curl -XPOST https://control-plane.internal/api/tenants/maplepay/policies -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"batching": {"immediate_dequeue": true, "max_batch_size": 24}}'
```
maria-sre: Patch applied: maxDepth=1200, immediate_dequeue=true, max_batch_size=24. Monitoring.
alex-oncall: Post-change numbers: queue depth dropped from 820 -> 320 within 45s, error rate down to baseline. Customers reporting restored responses. :thumbsup:
sam-support: Customer update sent: "we applied a mitigation (queue policy + config) and are monitoring; please retry if you see errors, we'll follow up with a permanent plan." MaplePay replied: thanks, they can hold while we validate.
ben-runtime: Next steps for root cause: - roll an AB back to 20ms or add tenant-aware batching defaults - add heuristics to detect heavy-KV-warmup requests and prioritize or isolate them - add a per-tenant slow-request breaker to avoid head-of-line blocking.
kevin-eng: I'll book a follow-up RFC to change tenant batching heuristics and a small rollout plan. Also propose an autoscale policy for batcher workers when queue_depth > 70% for 60s.
maria-sre: Logging note: we should capture batch-level diagnostic metrics (per-batch slowest-item-ms, kv-miss-count) to make these incidents easier to triage.
alex-oncall: Closing loop: incident mitigated, customer stable, follow-ups assigned to eng-runtime and SRE. I'll file the postmortem link here once written.
ben-runtime: 👍
sam-support: thanks team.
